newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends steady, still seeking direction.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends steady, still seeking direction.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures ended steady after drifting sideways for much of the days looking for fresh direction from NYMEX crude and products, none of which came, traders said.
March Brent last traded three cents up at $22.46 a barrel.
The contract slipped back a little in early trade, extending Tuesday's late losses but recovered later as the market shrugged off mixed U.S. oil stocks data from the API.
"There's was nothing at-all out there today worth moving on -- NYMEX didn't go anywhere and there was no news to drive it." one broker said.
"Even the news that the EIA had hiked it's Q1 oil price forecast failed to impress the U.S. market," another said.
The EIA revised it's forecast for Q1 1997 U.S. oil prices, including imports up $1.38 a barrel to and average $23.18.
Gas oil ended around mid-range after a lacklustre day's trading that saw the market fluctuate either side of $200.

Traders said business remained nervous and directionless after dipping in early trade on U.S. stocks data showing year-ago stock levels for U.S. distillates had moved into surplus for the first time since June 1995.
The Feb contract ended $2 down at $201 a tonne.

The Feb/March backwardation, the focus of attention for both spot and futures traders because of a perceived squeeze by one U.S. trade house, narrowed slightly to around $7.50 after stretching out to $10 on Tuesday.

Dealers said NYMEX heating oil was still very much in the driving seat as far as direction was concerned with ample supplies, lack of arbitrage opportunities and above normal temperatures in much of Europe keeping sentiment weak.
"You have to look at the products in the States to get a lead from them for the moment because volume is incredibly thin here (London)," one trader.
